project.description_en: At the end of the theme, the child shows a small album with drawings or photos of the family, names each person, shows one way to help at home and one safety rule in the kitchen.

activities.goal_en: Listen to a story, distinguish good and bad behaviour and draw a lesson.
activities.prompt_en: Listen: who helped Grandmother? Who did not help?
steps_en: Show a pot and say that Grandmother is cooking for the family.
Tell the story with the voices of the children.
Ask: who helped? Who did not? What happened at the end?
Ask the child how they help at home.
observe_en: Says who helped and who did not.
Gives one way of helping at home.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 14 (Storytelling: Short stories), p. 39; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.story_en: Grandmother was cooking a big pot of rice for the whole family. “Who will help me?” she asked. “Not me, I am playing,” said Fon. “I will!” said little Bih, and she brought water and washed the plates. When the food was ready, everybody came to eat. Grandmother smiled at Bih: “Thank you for helping. A family is strong when everyone helps.” The next day, Fon came first to bring the water.

activities.goal_en: Read pictures of family members and name them.
activities.prompt_en: Look at this picture. Who is it? Is it Mummy, Daddy, Grandma or the baby?
steps_en: Show photos or drawings of family members.
Point to each person and name them together.
Ask the child to find “the baby”, “the grandfather”.
Make a small album by sticking the pictures in order.
observe_en: Points to the right person when asked.
Turns the pages from front to back.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 17 (Reading: Picture reading), p. 42; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Draw raindrops and zigzag lines with control.
activities.prompt_en: Draw little raindrops: dot, dot, dot. Now the lightning: zig, zag, zig, zag!
steps_en: Make dots in the air, then on paper.
Draw a zigzag in the air, saying “zig, zag”.
Trace zigzags in sand with a finger.
Draw raindrops and zigzags on paper.
observe_en: Draws a zigzag with clear points.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 18 (Writing: Pre-letter formation), p. 43; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Say good evening and good night in French at home.
activities.prompt_en: In the evening, we say “Bonsoir !”. When we go to bed, we say “Bonne nuit !”.
steps_en: Show a picture of the evening: say “Bonsoir !”.
Show a picture of a bed: say “Bonne nuit !”.
The child repeats with gestures.
Act: the child says “Bonne nuit, Maman !” to a doll.
observe_en: Uses each at the right moment.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 19 (French: Salutations), p. 44; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Add two small groups and find how many in all, up to 5.
activities.prompt_en: Mummy has 2 oranges. Daddy gives her 3 more. How many oranges now?
steps_en: Put 2 oranges (or stones) on the table.
Add 3 more, one by one.
Count all of them together.
Try other small additions with the child.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 20 (Mathematics: Mathematical operations), p. 45; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

interactive.prompt_en: 2 oranges and 3 more oranges. How many oranges in all?
interactive.explanation_en: Put them together and count: one, two, three, four, five. There are 5 oranges.

activities.goal_en: Compare and sort household objects by size.
activities.prompt_en: Which pot is big? Which is small? Put the big things here and the small things there.
steps_en: Show two pots: a big one and a small one.
Say “big” and “small” with gestures.
Give the child cups, spoons and plates of different sizes.
Sort them into big and small.
materials_en: big and small pots, cups, spoons
source_refs: Nursery One, table 20 (Mathematics: Classifying elements), p. 45; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Locate natural and artificial sources of light and stay away from dangerous ones.
activities.prompt_en: What gives light in the day? And at night in our house?
steps_en: Go outside: the sun gives light in the day.
Inside, show a torch and a lamp (switched off).
Talk about candles and fire: only adults light them.
Switch the torch on and off with an adult.
observe_en: Names the sun as a source of light.
Names one light in the house.
Says that fire and candles are for adults.
materials_en: pictures of the sun and a candle
source_refs: Nursery One, table 22 (Science and Technology: Sources of light), p. 47–48; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Follow safety rules in the kitchen and protect oneself from danger.
activities.prompt_en: In the kitchen, the fire and the pots are hot. We stay away from the fire and we do not touch knives.
steps_en: Show a picture of a kitchen.
Point to dangers: the fire, a hot pot, a knife, a pot handle.
Say one rule for each danger.
Act: the child stays at a safe distance while an adult cooks.
observe_en: Says one rule (stay away from the fire).
Stays away from the pretend fire.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 27 (Safety Education: Home safety), p. 53; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Wash hands, wait for others, eat calmly and say thank you at the table.
activities.prompt_en: At the table, we wash our hands, wait for everyone, eat calmly and say thank you.
steps_en: Wash hands before sitting.
Wait until everyone is served.
Eat with the mouth closed, without shouting.
Say “thank you” for the food.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 25 (Character Education: Simple etiquettes), p. 51; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Help to keep the home clean and sort waste.
activities.prompt_en: Peels go in this bucket for the garden. Papers and plastics go in that bin.
steps_en: Show two containers: one for peels and leaves, one for papers and plastics.
Give the child clean waste to sort.
Throw each item in the right container.
Wash hands after.
observe_en: Puts papers and plastics in the bin.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 26 (Environmental Education: The environment), p. 52; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Mould a simple object with clay or dough.
activities.prompt_en: Roll a ball of clay, then press your thumb in the middle to make a little cup.
steps_en: Give a ball of clay or dough.
Roll it between the hands.
Press the thumb in the middle and turn.
Smooth the edges and let it dry.
observe_en: Makes a hollow with the thumb.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 31 (Handwork: Practice sessions), p. 57; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Play a team game carrying objects to a basket.
activities.prompt_en: Each team carries the oranges, one by one, to its basket. Ready? Go!
steps_en: Make two teams and two baskets.
Each child carries one object to the basket and runs back.
The next child goes.
Count the objects in each basket together and say well done.
observe_en: Carries the object without dropping it.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 32 (Physical Education and Sports: Team sports), p. 58; theme 3: The family and home (table 13, p. 37)

scale.description: Succeeds mostly with a model or help.
Sometimes succeeds alone, sometimes with a reminder.
Succeeds on their own in a familiar situation.

indicators: Names the members of their family.
Retells a short story with help.
Adds two small groups up to 5.
Says one danger in the kitchen.
Helps to sort waste at home.

sources: Cameroon Nursery School Curriculum, English Subsystem, MINEDUB, 2018: table 13 (integrated learning themes), p. 37; Nursery One tables, cited and not reproduced.
